title: Fallback Graph Exchange — proto draft
content:
Context and intent:

This is a lightweight, transport-neutral spec for exchanging compact fallback graphs between components (ingress, policy engine, route manager, and per-tenant caches). Purpose: make fallback logic explicit, serializable, and cheaply diff-able so rollouts, audits, and cross-region sync are straightforward.

Why: current fallback behavior is embedded in code paths and ad-hoc config blobs. Hard to reason about multi-step fallbacks (model variant -> region -> degrade-to-embedding -> queue-and-retry). We want a small schema that:
- expresses ordered and parallel fallback steps
- allows conditional edges based on telemetry (latency, error class, recent QPS)
- supports weighted/percentage splits for gradual rollouts and A/B
- carries lightweight provenance (source, version, timestamp)

Non-goals: full policy language, complex rate-limits (refer to Admission Control), or OPA-like evaluation. Keep it pragmatic for the runtime.

1) Core concepts (v0)
- Node: an action node. Types: call_model, route_region, fallback_to_cache, degrade_quality, enqueue_retry, respond_with_stub, escalate_to_dedicated. Each node has an id (short string) and metadata.
- Edge: directional link from node A -> node B with optional condition and weight.
- Graph: entry node id + node map + edge set + metadata (version, source).

2) Human-readable mini-DSL (for quick editing / testing)
Example:

graph: v=2026-02-20
entry: serve

nodes:
  serve: call_model(model="gptx-8k-q4f")
  fallback_local: fallback_to_cache(ttl=30s)
  degrade: degrade_quality(level="safety-first", temp=0.7)
  alt_model: call_model(model="gptx-8k-quant2")
  region_failover: route_region(region="eu-west-2")
  stall: enqueue_retry(max=2, backoff="200ms")
  respond_stub: respond_with_stub(template_id="safety_stub_v1")

edges:
  serve -> alt_model [cond: error in [TIMEOUT, OOM], weight=80%]
  serve -> fallback_local [cond: latency > 600ms, weight=100%]
  alt_model -> region_failover [cond: region_unavailable]
  alt_model -> degrade [cond: token_limit_exceeded]
  region_failover -> stall
  stall -> respond_stub [cond: attempts==max]

Notes: weights are used for controlled canaries. We interpret multiple outgoing edges with weights as probabilistic selection when conditions match. If no weights present, edges are deterministic (first-match).

3) JSON transport shape (flat, intentionally simple)
Purpose: canonical wire format for exchange (HTTP, gRPC metadata blob, etc.). Keep fields as strings/numbers/arrays only.

{
  "version": "v0.1",
  "id": "fallback-graph-tenant-42-20260220",
  "entry": "serve",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "serve", "type": "call_model", "meta": "model=gptx-8k-q4f;timeout=400ms" },
    { "id": "alt_model", "type": "call_model", "meta": "model=gptx-8k-quant2;timeout=600ms" },
    { "id": "fallback_local", "type": "fallback_to_cache", "meta": "ttl=30s" },
    { "id": "stall", "type": "enqueue_retry", "meta": "max=2;backoff=200ms" },
    { "id": "respond_stub", "type": "respond_with_stub", "meta": "template=safety_stub_v1" }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "from": "serve", "to": "alt_model", "cond": "error in [TIMEOUT, OOM]", "weight_pct": "80" },
    { "from": "serve", "to": "fallback_local", "cond": "latency>600", "weight_pct": "100" },
    { "from": "alt_model", "to": "stall" },
    { "from": "stall", "to": "respond_stub", "cond": "attempts==max" }
  ],
  "meta": "source:runtime/route-manager@rev:1823;created_at:2026-02-20T14:12:00Z"
}

Implementation notes:
- Nodes.meta is semicolon-delimited k=v pairs to avoid nested objects in tiny exchange blobs. Parsers provide helpers.
- Conditions are tiny boolean-expr strings evaluated by the policy engine; keep grammar minimal (comparators, membership, simple math).
- Weight_pct stored as integer string 0-100. Default deterministic semantics unless multiple edges sum >0.

4) APIs to exchange graphs
- GET /v1/fallback-graph/{tenant_id}  -> returns latest graph for tenant (200 + JSON)
- POST /v1/fallback-graph/{tenant_id}  -> upload new graph (requires signature; returns 202 + id)
- PATCH /v1/fallback-graph/{tenant_id}/diff -> apply small edge/node patches (optimistic concurrency)
- GET /v1/fallback-graph/{tenant_id}/eval?context={encoded} -> dry-run evaluation outcome for telemetry/preview

Security/consistency:
- Signed manifests (kms-sig) for production graphs. Untrusted graphs (dev) allowed when header X-Runtime-Debug=true.
- Version monotonicity required. Servers should reject graphs with lower version unless override flag.
- Small size target: keep < 2KB for most graphs. If >2KB, store pointer to object store and keep metadata inline.

5) Observability hooks (where we record telemetry)
Emit event on: graph_applied, graph_rejected, node_taken, edge_chosen(weight), evaluation_preview. Attach compact provenance: graph_id, source, applied_by, server_region, decision_path (comma-delimited node ids).

6) Runtime evaluation semantics (quick draft)
- Start at entry node. At each node: attempt action. Evaluate outgoing edges in order: filter by condition (if any). If multiple edges remain with weight_pct > 0, pick probabilistically according to weights. If a deterministic edge exists (weight_pct omitted or 0), follow it. If no edges, return node's default outcome (success/response/error).
- Short-circuit: when node type is respond_with_stub or escalate_to_dedicated, stop.

7) Edge cases and open questions (TODOs)
- How to express compound conditions (eg: latency > 500ms AND recent_error_rate > 2%) without making grammar heavy? Poss: accept simple and provide a hook to call an external evaluator (policy service).
- Backwards compatibility for older agents that expect legacy blobs. Need small compatibility layer (transformer).
- Interactions with per-route batching: if we fallback to cache, do we still count tokens for billing? (billing team Q)
- Deterministic replay for audits: need a seed + recorded random choices for weighted edges. Where to keep? (Edge: store in trace ID payload)
- Should we allow subgraphs (include/import) to share common patterns? Pro: reuse; Con: increases fetch complexity.

8) Mini roadmap
- v0.1: wire-format + runtime eval + GET/POST + simple signature verify (Q1 2026)
- v0.2: PATCH/diff, preview API, telemetry enrichment (Q2 2026)
- v0.3: import/include, policy-evaluator hook, canary split scheduler (Q3 2026)

Appendix: example decision trace (text)
trace_id: t-9a3f
path: serve -> alt_model (edge weight chosen=80) -> stall -> respond_stub
emit: node_taken=serve;edge_chosen=serve->alt_model;node_taken=alt_model;edge_chosen=alt_model->stall;node_taken=stall;node_taken=respond_stub

Quick integration notes for onboarding:
- route-manager: fetch graph on attach, cache TTL 30s, watch for config push notifications from control plane.
- policy-engine: evaluate conditions with local metrics; fallback to control-plane evaluation if expression uses uncommon metrics.
- ingress: prefer local quick-check cache before making remote graph lookup.

If we like this shape I will:
- write small python/golang serializer + validator
- add Linear ticket for signature integration and review: RW-XXXX
- prototype trace attachments + SDK helper for recording chosen-edge

Unresolved: I intentionally left meta as a small object in example JSON — production file must keep meta flat per agents.md but control-plane can sign the whole blob.

Notes-to-self (brain dump)
- Keep parser simple: semicolon meta, lightweight expr grammar. Avoid nested JSON in nodes to reduce parsing overhead at ingress.
- Experiment: include compact fingerprint (sha256 hex) in graph id to detect accidental duplicates.
- Perf target: evaluation < 50us on p95 path for simple graphs.

End of draft.
